text_2:
Learn to reason.
Learn to question evidence.
text_3:
Graduate teaching assistant
UNLV · Since Fall 2024
text_4: Since Fall 2024, I have supported undergraduate statistics and calculus at UNLV through discussion instruction, course materials, office hours, and tutoring. Working with course instructors, I help students connect concepts with problem-solving and explain their reasoning. My responsibilities vary by course and semester.
text_5: The assignments below are graduate assistant / teaching assistant appointments. Discussion instruction is carried out in collaboration with the course instructor.
text_7: From a meaningful question to a defensible conclusion.
text_8: My goal is to help students become thoughtful users of data: able to ask a clear question, examine how evidence was collected, recognize variability, and explain what an analysis can and cannot establish. I connect intuitive explanations and visual representations with mathematical reasoning, so that procedures have a purpose and conclusions remain grounded in context.
text_9: I aim to organize statistics discussions around investigation: question, data, exploration, inference, and communication. Real examples from health and everyday life can make decisions about sampling, measurement, confounding, and missing data visible. Simulation offers a bridge from informal ideas about chance to sampling distributions, randomization tests, and confidence intervals; formulas then deepen that understanding.
text_10: A supportive classroom also needs intellectual challenge. I encourage questions and treat mistakes as opportunities to diagnose reasoning. My teaching development priorities include structured peer discussion, brief checks of understanding, scaffolded computing, and clear feedback. I seek to make participation accessible through readable materials, multiple representations, and opportunities to think before speaking.
text_11: Assessment should reveal understanding as well as procedural accuracy. I aim to align tasks with explicit learning goals and ask students to justify a method, interpret uncertainty, and critique a conclusion. For example, a correct calculation should be accompanied by an explanation of the population, assumptions, and limits of the inference. Short written explanations and transfer problems can expose misconceptions that a numerical answer alone misses.
text_12: Responsible analysis is part of statistical literacy. My teaching goals include reproducible workflows, transparent data provenance, privacy, and a careful distinction between association and causation. Where course policy permits AI tools, students should disclose their use, verify outputs, and explain the reasoning themselves. Technology should support learning without replacing judgment.
text_13: I view teaching as an ongoing process of inquiry. I plan to use student questions, formative assessments, peer feedback, and reflective notes to refine discussion activities with the course instructor. These commitments draw on ASA GAISE guidance and statistics education research; the approaches below describe my continuing development rather than a claim that every method has already been implemented.
text_15: A focused reading shelf for my development as a statistics educator. Start with the ASA guidance and a practical activity book, then connect each reading to one discussion activity and one assessment question. These are selected resources, not a universal ranking.
text_16: A sustainable cycle: define one learning goal → choose a task → check students’ reasoning → revise. Keep reusable lesson notes, record the source and license of borrowed materials, and review this reading list each academic year.

resources.title: ASA GAISE College Report
resources.author: American Statistical Association · living report
resources.description: Guidance for introductory statistics and data science, including learning outcomes, assessment examples, and a section on AI. Use it to audit a lesson’s goals, activity, and assessment.
resources.access: Free online · Consult the living report for updates.

resources.title: The Introductory Statistics Course: A Ptolemaic Curriculum?
resources.author: George W. Cobb · 2007
resources.description: A foundational argument for rethinking introductory inference. Teaching task: let students explore a randomization distribution before introducing a formal test.

resources.title: Data Science in Statistics Curricula: Preparing Students to “Think with Data”
resources.author: Hardin and colleagues · 2015
resources.description: Examples of integrating data science into statistics curricula. Teaching task: build a small exercise that joins data cleaning, visualization, interpretation, and reproducible code.
resources.access: Free author manuscript · Published in The American Statistician.

resources.title: Teaching and Learning Data Visualization: Ideas and Assignments
resources.author: Deborah Nolan & Jamis Perrett · 2016
resources.description: Ideas for making graphics part of statistical education. Teaching task: ask students to revise a misleading plot and explain how the revised design supports the statistical question.
resources.access: Free author manuscript · Published in The American Statistician.

resources.title: Teaching Statistics: A Bag of Tricks
resources.author: Andrew Gelman & Deborah Nolan · 2nd edition, 2017
resources.description: My first choice for practical teaching preparation: classroom examples and activities, including topics for more advanced courses. Adapt one activity to a specific learning goal rather than adding it only for entertainment.
resources.access: Publisher preview · Check institutional access or borrowing.

resources.title: Developing Students’ Statistical Reasoning: Connecting Research and Teaching Practice
resources.author: Garfield, Ben-Zvi, Chance, Medina, Roseth & Zieffler · 2008
resources.description: A deeper research foundation for teaching variability, distributions, inference, and modeling. Start with the chapters on learning environments and assessment, then select a concept you currently teach.
resources.access: Publisher preview · Check institutional access or borrowing.

resources.title: Introduction to Modern Statistics
resources.author: Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel & Johanna Hardin · 2nd edition
resources.description: A course-design model for exploratory analysis, multivariable thinking, simulation, and traditional inference. Use the R tutorials and labs as inspiration for scaffolded discussions.
resources.link_label: Read the book and teaching resources ↗
resources.access: Free web text and PDF · Some instructor resources require verification.

resources.title: Computational and Inferential Thinking: The Foundations of Data Science
resources.author: Ani Adhikari, John DeNero & David Wagner
resources.description: A complementary Python-based model for teaching computation alongside inference. Explore an example of simulation or resampling and adapt the statistical idea to your students’ computing background.

resources.title: CAUSEweb: resources, research, and professional development
resources.author: Consortium for the Advancement of Undergraduate Statistics Education
resources.description: A continuing source of teaching activities and professional learning. Use the core readings index to follow a topic in depth and evaluate activities against your own course goals.
resources.access: Free resource hub · Includes simulation-based inference and teaching networks.

text_17: Biomedical methods: visualize, compute, and explain
text_18: A learning pathway connecting statistical theory with biomedical questions. These resources support my developing interests; listing a method does not imply that I have used it in a completed study.

biomedical.title: Causal Inference: What If + DAGitty
biomedical.author: Hernán & Robins · Textbook and causal diagram software
biomedical.description: Define a treatment effect and draw the assumed causal structure before fitting a model. Practice identification, standardization, weighting, and sensitivity to unmeasured confounding using a biomedical example.
biomedical.access: Companion tool: dagitty.net · Graphs encode assumptions; they do not establish them.

biomedical.title: Regression Modeling Strategies
biomedical.author: Frank E. Harrell Jr. · Course notes, book, and R rms ecosystem
biomedical.description: Study flexible regression, survival outcomes, missing data, overfitting, and validation. Practice a clinical risk model with nonlinear effects; visualize calibration and assess performance before interpreting it.
biomedical.access: Free online notes · Book is separate · R packages rms and Hmisc.

biomedical.title: Disease transmission modeling in Stan
biomedical.author: Stan case study · Bayesian SIR modeling
biomedical.description: A direct connection to epidemic-modeling interests: inspect an SIR model, simulate observations, fit it, and examine posterior predictive checks and computational diagnostics. Distinguish uncertainty in parameters from uncertainty in predictions.
biomedical.access: Free case study · Requires probability, Bayesian inference, and computing foundations.

biomedical.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
biomedical.author: James and colleagues · R and Python editions
biomedical.description: Build foundations in regularization, resampling, classification, and flexible prediction. Biomedical practice: compare a transparent baseline with a more flexible model using leakage-free validation, calibration, and clinically meaningful error measures.
biomedical.access: Free PDFs and companion labs · Predictive performance alone does not identify a causal effect.

biomedical.title: Targeted Learning in R
biomedical.author: tlverse · Reproducible methods handbook
biomedical.description: After causal identification and estimation basics, study how targeted estimation combines machine learning with inference for a defined parameter. Practice TMLE and investigate how nuisance estimation, positivity, and sample splitting affect inference.
biomedical.access: Free online · Advanced pathway; check software documentation before reproducing examples.

biomedical.title: Bioconductor workflows and OSCA
biomedical.author: Bioconductor · Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis
biomedical.description: Explore quality control, normalization, biological replication, dimension reduction, and multiple testing. Biomedical practice: reproduce a public workflow and explain how batch effects and the choice of experimental unit influence conclusions.
biomedical.access: Free R ecosystem · Companion book: osca.bioconductor.org.

biomedical.title: Asymptotic Statistics
biomedical.author: A. W. van der Vaart · Graduate theory
biomedical.description: Develop the foundations behind estimation and uncertainty: likelihood, M-estimation, asymptotic efficiency, bootstrap methods, and semiparametric theory. Pair a derivation with simulation of estimator bias and interval coverage.
biomedical.access: Publisher access · Requires substantial probability and mathematical statistics preparation.

biomedical.title: R for Data Science + Quarto
biomedical.author: Wickham, Çetinkaya-Rundel & Grolemund · Open text and publishing tools
biomedical.description: Build reliable data import, cleaning, visualization, and reporting habits. Practice one biomedical analysis in a Quarto document with a data dictionary, documented exclusions, seeds, package versions, diagnostic plots, and a clear interpretation.
